content.thinking:
I'm planning the full file structure, using the builder API with imports for THREE, paints, rng, and a toon shader kit, designing a chunky dwarf figure around 1.3 meters tall.

Working out exact proportions in meters—boots, legs, barrel torso, pauldrons, and an oversized helmeted head with a beard reaching down to the chest—then sketching helper functions for boxes, spheres, and rods to keep geometry calls concise. I'm also settling on a color palette: ruddy skin, fiery beard, steel-blue armor, brown leather, deep blue cloth, gold trim, and dark iron accents, all mapped through cel-shaded paints.

Now I'm figuring out how to build the braided beard using a path-based approach, stepping along a catmull curve with spheres of shrinking radius and alternating rotation to simulate braid links, capped with gold clasps, while the main beard mass gets built from scaled overlapping spheres and a tapering spike shape.

For the texture, I'm layering a grain pattern wrapped in cel-shading to give the beard a hairy strand look, then moving on to the face details — a skin-toned head sphere, oversized nose, small eyes with pupils, bushy rotated-box eyebrows, and swirled mustache capsules — before designing a lathed steel helmet with a gold trim band and small horn-like spikes for a dwarf aesthetic.

Writing lathe outline points...

I'm adding a ring of ten small rivet spheres around the helmet band using trig positioning, then building the torso as a scaled barrel cylinder painted blue with cel-shaded stripes for the tunic, plus a flattened steel chest plate and a gold torus trim.

Now I'm shaping a leather belt cylinder with a gold buckle box, sized to match the torso radius, then adding shoulder pauldrons as flattened steel spheres with gold rim toruses, and upper arm rods running from shoulder to elbow positions.

For the gun, I'm positioning the blunderbuss diagonally across the body at port arms, with the right hand gripping near the stock and left hand forward under the barrel—working out butt and muzzle coordinates so the weapon angles up and forward at roughly 20 degrees.

Building the gun geometry...

Setting the stock butt end tapering from a wider wooden grip to a narrower neck, and applying a wood grain texture with alternating brown tones along the direction vector.

Now I'm positioning the hands on the grip: right hand just below the lock mechanism, left hand under the barrel with a slight downward offset for a ball-grip pose, and I'm computing the normalized direction vector to place the forearm and elbow joints relative to the hand positions along the stock's axis.

I'm also planning the leg geometry -- thighs as rods running from hip to knee with brown pants material, continuing to build out the lower body skeleton.

Next I'm positioning the boots: box shapes for toe, cuff, heel, and sole pieces so the sole sits flush at floor level, with the boot top meeting the trouser rod. I'm also adding kneepad spheres and sketching gear like a backpack sack, bedroll, and powder horn built from a swept curved shape.

Then I plan out a bandolier strap sweeping diagonally across the chest from shoulder to hip, following the torso's elliptical curve, with small boxes for pouches and a row of cylindrical cartridge loops spaced along the strap path.

I decide to skip the big chest plate and emblem in favor of a simpler tunic, leather vest, and gold buckle, adding pauldrons and a gorget instead. For the back, I'm placing a leather backpack box with a cylindrical bedroll strapped across the top, rotated to lie horizontally.

Still writing accessories and face features...

I'm mapping out the beard shape with a central spike and two side braids hanging down the chest, nudging the z-depth forward so they sit visibly on top of the torso instead of embedding inside it, with the beard colored orange cel-shaded with grain texture.

Now I'm working out the ears as small rounded balls beneath the helmet, then sizing the helmet itself to clear the head's curvature — widening its base radius and height, and adding a small gold spike crest at the top to bring the total figure height up to about 1.4m, roughly in proportion for a dwarf.

Settling on 1.4m with the floor at y=0, I'm adding helmet trim: a gold brim torus, curved bone-colored side horns built from a swept catmull path tapering outward and upward, and a small steel nasal guard box positioned at the face.

Then for the pauldrons, I'm placing scaled gold spheres at each shoulder with a tilted rim torus for the gold trim, keeping the rotation flat along the XZ plane.

For rivets, I'm looping gold ball positions around the ring angles, then adding a steel gorget torus around the neck that the beard mostly covers. For the torso, I'm using a mottled blue cel-shaded cylinder for the tunic, and considering a second slightly larger cylinder for the leather vest, open-ended to avoid odd cap geometry.

I'm computing the torso cylinder with its position and z-scale, then adding a slightly offset belly sphere scaled for a rounded bulge to give the figure some shape.

The belly ball's coverage looks borderline at that angle, so I'll skip it and instead widen the torso at the bottom to compensate. For the strap path, I'm computing z-offsets along the torso surface at each x-position so the strap sits flush against the body rather than floating.

I'm adjusting the strap's last point since it was outside the torso radius, then adding belt pouches as small leather boxes with flaps at both hips, plus considering a hatchet or small axe hanging at the left hip for extra detail.

Now I'm keeping the hatchet simple with just a rod handle and box-shaped head, moving on to boot details with mottled brown paint and small gold buckle straps at the ankles, then adding steel vambrace segments on the forearms using a lerp helper, and I'm setting up a reusable arm-building function that constructs capsule shapes from shoulder to elbow to hand.

I'm recalculating the left arm joint positions since the dwarf's proportions came out too stretched—shortening the forearm and upper-arm distances so the elbow and hand placements feel proportionally correct.

Now I'm working through the right arm with similar length checks, then adding the weapon details: a steel lock box, a small angled gold hammer piece, and a thin rod loop for the trigger guard.

Still writing gun geometry...

Adding a ramrod beneath the barrel and a gold engraving line along the top, keeping the hand-painted cel style with modest part count (~150) using loops for studs and rivets. I'll skip extra embellishments like glow effects, runes, gems, and fur texture cards to avoid rendering risks, though I consider a simple sphere-ring fur mantle as an alternative.

Checking which imports I actually need—keeping THREE, createBuilder, catmull, and the paint functions mottle, grain, stripes, plus cel and INK for toon shading—while dropping unused ones like rng and glow to satisfy TypeScript strictness.

I'll define a helper point function returning fixed 3-number arrays offset from a base position along a direction vector, set up metadata fields, and use a mirror loop over [1,-1] for symmetric left/right placement. Time to start writing the actual code now.

Writing part helper functions...

Adjusting braid z-depth so it overlaps the torso without clipping, then adding gold rings, a clasp, and tassel at the braid's end, plus a red ribbon bow. Also recalculating eye z-position against the head's curvature.

I need to adjust cheek placement so they poke through the beard sphere rather than being fully hidden—repositioning them slightly to stay visible against the beard's curvature. The mustache sits comfortably over the beard front at that height.

For the helmet hair tufts, backpack, and bedroll, I'm placing orange sideburn balls scaled to the beard shape, positioning the backpack box against the torso's back slightly embedded, and adding a rotated cylinder for the bedroll with torus-ring straps and a flap box to finish the look.

Now I'm adding smaller accessories: a steel pot cylinder near the hip, skipping the hatchet for simplicity, placing a tankard with a handle torus at the belt, and sizing a pouch box angled against the torso curve using the circle equation to find proper depth.

I'm positioning gold stud balls around the leather belt and arranging a fur collar ring of twelve balls at the neckline, then double-checking that the boots and other elements stay within a reasonable footprint.

Now I'm detailing the boot geometry: rounded toe caps, flat soles, boxed uppers, and leather cuffs, then connecting them with rod-shaped legs up to hip-filling pants geometry in a brown-blue tone.

Adding kneepad details...
